A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the expression level of MAGE‐C1 and MAGE‐A3/A6/A9/A10/A12 genes was significantly higher in the peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from patients with lung cancer compared to the PBMCs from healthy donors.
the expression of MAGE‐ A1 and MAGE‐A3/6 in the peripheral blood is a poor prognosticator in patients with lung cancer.

we found that the MAGE‐A gene family was expressed in the peripheral blood mononuclear cells of patients with lung carcinoma, and the expression of the MAGE‐C1 and MAGE‐C2 genes was correlated with poor prognosis of lung cancer patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MAGE‐A1 and MAGE‐A3 gene expression in the peripheral white blood cells of patients with non‐small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is a poor prognosticator of overall survival.
the expression of MAGE‐ A1, A2 and A4 genes in the peripheral blood is a significant and independent prognostic factor for overall survival (OS) in patients with lung cancer.

the expression of MAGE‐C1, MAGE‐C2 and MAGE‐C3 in peripheral blood is associated with poor overall survival in lung cancer patients, and MAGE‐A gene expressions are independent prognostic markers for overall survival in lung cancers.
